upstream.label: is interrupted when scope is closed

cases.behavior: Closing an owning scope interrupts its child and waits for child cleanup before parent cleanup.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: The Ergo fixture asserts completed child-before-parent release, not upstream Scope internals or the entire forkScoped API.

upstream.label: scoped combines usage and finalizer failures

cases.behavior: An expected failure and a cleanup defect both survive scope closure.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo uses Timeout plus an acquired-resource cleanup defect, including attempted Timeout recovery. This is a behavior comparison, not a port of generic addFinalizer syntax.

upstream.label: sleep - does not require passage of wall time

cases.behavior: Advancing test program time admits an already-forked sleeper and allows its join without waiting for the requested wall-clock delay.
cases.limits: Ergo's TestClock is std time's Manual (std-align S2b), which provides Scheduler and time.Clock. TestTimeEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_time_test.go) starts a task that sleeps 10 hours on a Manual, advances the Manual 11 hours, and waits for the task; the Go test bounds the run to 30 seconds of wall time. Effect's adjust also runs the woken fibers before it returns; Advance wakes the sleepers, and the program reads the task's result with Wait. The program waits until the task is asleep (Sleepers) before it advances. The case lost its earlier evidence with the .ef compiler (#205).

upstream.label: sleep - delays effects until time is adjusted

cases.behavior: A sleeper of 10 hours is still asleep after the test clock moves 9 hours, and it ends after the clock moves 11 hours more.
cases.limits: On std time's Manual (std-align S2b). Effect polls the fiber; Ergo reads Sleepers (1 after 9 hours) and then waits for the task, and Sleepers is 0 after it ends. TestTimeEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_time_test.go) checks it.

cases.behavior: Two sleepers of 3 hours and 1 hour wake in deadline order: after the clock moves 1 hour only the shorter one has run, and after 4 hours more both have.
cases.limits: On std time's Manual (std-align S2b). Effect's sleepers append to one shared string; Ergo's tasks return their parts, and the program joins them in the order the tasks end. TestTimeEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_time_test.go) checks it.

cases.behavior: A deadline reports a typed timeout; a timer defect must retain its Cause rather than being recast as that timeout.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream asserts Cause.TimeoutError with a duration message. Ergo declares nominal Timeout and an explicit Scheduler capability; its supplemental invalid-duration timer test also checks cleanup defects. This does not claim identical timeout APIs or full upstream case parity.

cases.behavior: Interrupt during protected acquisition skips use but releases the acquired resource.
cases.limits: Generic source-level acquisition callback contracts and causal acquisition-boundary acceptance remain future owned-core work; existing lifecycle providers are not this proof.

cases.behavior: The first completion wins; repeated completion returns false and waiters see the first value.
cases.limits: An internal latch is not an admitted generic Ergo Deferred API. Recipe execution/memoization is separate from single assignment and does not imply concurrent producer single-flight.

cases.behavior: A Ref read returns its current stored value.
cases.limits: Generic mutable payload ownership and callback purity admission remain required; native cells alone are not source-level conformance.

cases.behavior: Sorting by the natural order of numbers gives a new sorted array; an empty array gives an empty one.
cases.limits: Ergo's slices.Sort (std-align S2a) is Go's slices.Sort over a copy: it returns a new slice, and the input keeps its order, as Effect's sort does. Ergo has no Set, so the upstream Set inputs have no port. TestStdSlicesEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_slices_test.go) checks the array inputs.

cases.behavior: Mapping a function over an array gives the array of its results, in order.
cases.limits: Ergo's name is slices.Transform (std-align S2a; Map is the prelude's map type), and its callback takes the element only, so Effect's second case, whose callback takes the index, has no port. TestStdSlicesEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_slices_test.go) checks the first case.

cases.behavior: Filtering keeps the elements the predicate accepts, in order: odd numbers of [1, 2, 3], and the present options of a list of options.
cases.limits: Ergo's slices.Filter (std-align S2a) takes a predicate of the element only, so Effect's last case, whose predicate takes the index, has no port. TestStdSlicesEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_slices_test.go) checks the other three cases.

cases.behavior: Reducing from an initial value applies the function left to right: the strings a, b and c reduce to abc.
cases.limits: Ergo's name is slices.Fold (std-align S2a), and its function takes the accumulator and the element only, so Effect's second case, whose function takes the index, has no port. TestStdSlicesEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_slices_test.go) checks the first case.

upstream.label: next - generates a number between 0 inclusive and 1 exclusive

cases.behavior: A draw of the next random number is at least 0 and below 1.
cases.limits: Ergo's name is Random.Float64 (std-align S2c), after Go's math/rand/v2. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) draws 1000 numbers from the host provider rand.NewHost() and 1000 from rand.Seeded(8), where Effect draws one from its default provider.

upstream.label: nextBoolean - is deterministic with the same seed

cases.behavior: Three random booleans drawn under one seed are the same three booleans when the same seed is drawn again.
cases.limits: Ergo's Random has no Boolean draw, as Go's math/rand/v2 has none; the program draws Effect's nextBoolean, Random.Float64() > 0.5. Ergo's seed is a uint64 (rand.Seeded(25)), not a string. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) also holds the booleans equal to the reference model, Go's r.Float64() > 0.5 on rand.New(rand.NewPCG(25, v1.RandSeedHi)).

upstream.label: shuffle - returns a shuffled copy of all values

cases.behavior: Shuffling 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 gives the same values in some order, and the input keeps its order.
cases.limits: Ergo's rand.Shuffle (std-align S2c) returns a new slice, as Effect's shuffle does. Ergo slices have no reference identity to compare, so Effect's notStrictEqual has no port; the subtest checks that the input is unchanged. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) checks it under rand.Seeded(175) and sorts the output with slices.Sort.

upstream.label: shuffle - is deterministic with the same seed

cases.behavior: Shuffling 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 under one seed gives the same order when the same seed is used again.
cases.limits: Ergo's seed is a uint64 (rand.Seeded(185)), not a string. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) also holds the order equal to the reference model, Go's r.Shuffle on rand.New(rand.NewPCG(185, v1.RandSeedHi)).

upstream.label: choice - fails with NoSuchElementError for an empty iterable

cases.behavior: A random choice from an empty collection has no element to give.
cases.limits: Difference: Effect's choice fails with NoSuchElementError; Ergo's rand.Choice (std-align S2c) returns Option, and an empty slice gives None, with no failure in its row, as Ergo's slices.Min does. The caller must match None, so the empty case is still handled. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) checks the None, and that the choice draws nothing from the stream.

upstream.label: choice - is deterministic with the same seed

cases.behavior: Three random choices from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 under one seed are the same three values when the same seed is used again.
cases.limits: Ergo's seed is a uint64 (rand.Seeded(217)), not a string. TestRandEffectCases's subtest of this case (internal/sketch/lower/std_rand_test.go) also holds the values equal to the reference model, Go's r.IntN(5) on rand.New(rand.NewPCG(217, v1.RandSeedHi)).

cases.behavior: Interrupting queued permit acquisition does not consume or leak permits.
cases.limits: Future fixed-capacity Semaphore must add causal queued/handoff/cancel tests. PartitionedSemaphore and resize/manual release cases do not establish that first profile.

cases.behavior: Explicit parallel finalizer execution.
cases.limits: Ergo's admitted owned cleanup is sequential; no selectable parallel scope-finalization policy is exposed.

cases.behavior: A detached child outlives interruption of its parent.
cases.limits: Ergo's first profile requires an owning scope; detached fibers remain unsupported.

upstream.label: interrupting a build does not hang current or later requesters

cases.behavior: Interrupting one requester of a shared layer acquisition leaves other current and later requesters able to complete.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream MemoMap builds in the first requester's fiber, so interrupting it completes the shared entry with that interruption for every waiter. Ergo producers belong to the provision build: cancelling one waiter abandons only its own wait, the producer continues, and every other waiter observes the actual shared outcome. Whole-build cancellation is the only static-surface trigger; the evidence drives the emitted Go runtime seam directly until a language caller exists.

upstream.label: layers can be acquired in parallel

cases.behavior: Independent selected nodes acquire concurrently; cancelling the build while one producer never completes still returns after every producer joins.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the cancelDuringConcurrentAcquisition trace: a cooperative producer observes cancellation, a masked concurrent acquisition completes late, nothing is released or returned before both join, and the cause is the caller's interruption alone. It drives the emitted Go runtime seam directly, not upstream Layer.merge.

upstream.label: preserves a failure when a shared layer build is interrupted

cases.behavior: When a sibling fails while a shared node is still being acquired and another node waits on it, the build fails with the actual failure; the abort-induced interruption of the shared node does not replace or fabricate it.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the partialFailureRollback trace: the pending shared producer is cancelled and joined, its waiter never constructs, rollback releases dependents first and the typed failure stays primary beside every cleanup defect. Only the fail case is exercised; defect primary selection is covered by the Go runtime suite.

cases.behavior: Interrupting a build releases every resource that some node acquired, including one whose uninterruptible acquisition completes after the interruption.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream only checks that acquired implies released after an arbitrary interruption point. Ergo fixes the interruption point while two producers run and asserts the exact release order and that the late acquisition is released exactly once.

upstream.label: finalizers with multiple layers with provideTo

cases.behavior: Node finalizers run after the provided program's, dependents before their dependencies.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Ergo asserts the programFailureWithCleanupDefects trace, which also requires every finalizer to run after a program failure and each cleanup defect to follow the program failure in close order. Independent nodes close sequentially in reverse canonical order; concurrent closure is permitted but not exercised.

cases.behavior: Separate provisions are separate builds with independent acquisition tables: a node is acquired again by each build, a failed build retains its one outcome and is retried only by a new explicit build, and a caller-owned borrowed resource stays open across both.
cases.limits: Its evidence tests were deleted with the earlier .ef compiler (#205); the case returns when a v1 test asserts it. Earlier limits: Upstream shares one MemoMap across builds so the second build reuses the first build's layer. Ergo has no shared or global memo map; explicit cross-build leases remain libraries with their own owning scope.

upstream.label: should keep variadic argument order when options are interleaved

cases.behavior: A flag may follow a positional argument; the positional arguments keep their order, and a repeated switch is accepted.
cases.limits: Ergo's flag (std-align S1d) takes Go's syntax otherwise: a bare -- ends the flags, a value flag takes the next argument whatever it is, and a repeated value flag keeps its last value. TestFlagMatchesGo's subtest of this case parses three interleaved lists with repeated switches; the test also checks interleaving against a written model on 3,000 generated lists, and TestFlagCommandsRun checks a flag after a subcommand's positional argument.

upstream.label: throws DuplicateOption when shared parent and child flags reuse a name

cases.behavior: A parent's shared flag and a child's flag of one name are refused with DuplicateOption when the command tree is built.
cases.limits: Ergo's flag has no shared parent flags: a command's Set holds its own flags, and a nested command parses Rest(v) with its own Set. Two flags of one name in one Set are not refused either (a known gap, stdlib.md flag 6).

cases.behavior: The lines of a text keep their line feed (and a carriage return before it); a last line with no line feed is a line; an empty text has no lines.
cases.limits: Ergo's strings.Lines (std-align S1c) is Go's strings.Lines, which matches linesWithSeparators; Effect's linesIterator, which drops the separators, has no Ergo function. TestStdTextRuns2's subtest of this case checks the upstream inputs; the test also runs the law StringsLinesRebuild.

cases.behavior: Every occurrence of a text is replaced.
cases.limits: Ergo's strings.ReplaceAll is Go's and takes a text, not a regular expression (Effect's second case). TestStdTextRuns2's subtest of this case checks the upstream input; the law ReplaceAllLength runs in runtime/v1 TestStdTextLaws.

cases.behavior: A numeric text parses to a number; NaN and the infinities parse as literals; an empty, blank or non-numeric text gives none.
cases.limits: Different by design (std-align S1c): Ergo's strconv.ParseFloat is Go's. It does not trim spaces (" 42 " fails Malformed, Effect gives 42), and it fails with a typed Malformed or OutOfRange where Effect returns an Option with no reason. "42", "3.14", "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity", "", "   " and "not a number" agree. TestStdTextRuns2's subtest of this case checks every upstream input.

cases.behavior: Joining the parts tmp and file.txt gives the path tmp/file.txt.
cases.limits: Ergo's filepath.Join is Go's path/filepath.Join over one slice of parts (Ergo has no variadic parameters), and it is a pure function, not an operation of a Path service, so no layer is bound. The separator is / (Linux and darwin are the targets; std-align S3a). TestFilepathRuns's subtest of this case checks the upstream input; the laws of filepath run in runtime/v1 TestFilepathLaws.

upstream.label: kills every process in a pipeline

cases.behavior: A stop of the caller of std exec Run ends every process of the program's pipeline, not only the program itself, before the call returns.
cases.limits: The subtest TestExecRuns/effect.child-process.kills-pipeline runs an Ergo program that stops a task whose exec runs the pipeline. Ergo kills the program's process group; Effect spawns each pipeline stage and kills them by its handle. A process that leaves the group (setsid) is not killed, by design.

upstream.label: poll returns Option for non-blocking take

cases.behavior: std queue Poll takes the front value without waiting: None on an empty queue, Some of the front value otherwise.
cases.limits: The subtest TestQueuePollRuns/effect.queue.poll-option runs an Ergo program that polls an empty queue, pushes, and polls the front. Ergo's Poll also takes the value of a Push that waits on a capacity-0 queue, and gives None on a closed, empty queue: None does not tell an open queue from a closed one.
